## P4 / H1 — n=24 per day; one new data point, and the statistic is NOT re-derived

10-09: budget **171.4**, extension **0.0**, error **−171.4**, traversal **229.5
= 1.34x** budget. A **zero-extension day**, so the error sits exactly at
**−budget**, its arithmetic floor — the maximum over-read this budget could
produce. It is the **2nd-largest over-read in the per-day record** behind 10-06's
−180.1. Last eight per-day: **+41.7, −66.5, −180.1, −97.8, +210.6, −171.4**
(and 09-29 −112.2, 09-30 −75.2 before them). `track.py` raw: per-DAY **+17.7**
(n=24), per-scan **+22.4** (n=27).

**The established finding stands and is not restated as something it is not.**
The budget has **no usable skill**, verified two ways: budget MAE **116.1** vs a
leave-one-out constant **98.3** (n=19), and **90.9** vs **75.5** ex-09-21
(n=18); above/below-mean **sign agreement 9 of 19**. The correlation sign is
**outlier-driven** — **−0.080** across all days, **+0.224** without 09-21 — so
the correct claim is **"no usable skill"**, *not* "inversely predictive", and it
must not be restated as a negative correlation. **H1's multiplier branch stays
closed.** P4 remains the live proposal, unchanged.

**New caveat, from D26 above:** the n=19 / n=18 samples those figures were
computed over **lost three more days today**. The direction of the conclusion is
unaffected — a constant beating the model by ~18pts of MAE does not reverse on
three days — but the figures themselves are no longer reproducible, which is the
third reason on file to persist graded outcomes.

## The regime call was formally undetermined and right anyway — 1 of 30 in the record

Price **30843.5**, flip **30876.7**, distance **33.2**. Board CFD/index offset
**43.1**. The regime test is a sign test on `price − flip`, and **33.2 < 43.1**:
at a zero basis the same scan reads **9.9 ABOVE** the flip and `bias_engine`
selects **STRATEGY 1 (fade)** instead of STRATEGY 2 — opposite instructions, and
STRATEGY 2 was worth ~180pts. The conversion arithmetic was independently
verified at scan time (Friday cash close 30883.15, NQ roll-forward, front
contract not rolled), so **43.1 is a real CFD-vs-cash basis, not a conversion
fault**.

**Census, all PRE_NY scans carrying both a flip and a board offset (n=30):**
`|px − flip| < |offset|` has occurred **once — 10-12**. Next closest: 09-30
(69.6 vs 37.7), 10-07 (82.6 vs 25.8). Every other scan clears its own conversion
uncertainty by 3x or more.

**Outcome:** the flip was touched at 13:00Z, exceeded by **0.7pts** across 490
minutes with 3 rejected re-tests, and price fell **149.9**. The read was right.
**Recorded as luck, not method** — a sign test whose input uncertainty exceeds
its margin is a coin flip that landed well. **n=1, nothing proposed.**
**Pre-registered test:** at the next occurrence of `|px − flip| < |offset|`,
record whether the regime read was right **before** looking at anything else.

## Board offset — THE PRE-REGISTERED THIRD-BREACH TEST, RUN, AND THE SELL-OFF HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED

The hypothesis under test: *the futures-implied cash reference is biased low in a
sell-off because futures lead and overshoot, so the offset widens as the market
falls.* **It does not survive the record.**

- **The drift table in the 10-14 review starts at 09-30 and therefore omits
  09-28's 45.9.** The breach series against the D6 ~40pt line is **09-28 45.9 ·
  10-12 43.1 · 10-14 41.8 · 10-15 77.6 — four, not three.**
- **Direction explains a little, magnitude explains nothing.** Across 27 PRE_NY
  days: down-roll days mean offset **+22.7** (median 23.4) vs up-roll days
  **+9.3** (median 8.8); r(offset, roll) = **−0.361**, R² 0.13. **Within the 13
  down-roll days, r(offset, |roll|) = +0.039.** The largest down roll in the
  record, **09-14 NQ −525.5**, produced offset **−12.2** — opposite sign, near the
  bottom of the series. A correction scaled to the overnight move would have
  pushed that conversion the wrong way by tens of points.
- **A time trend dominates:** r(offset, sequence) = **+0.607**, slope **+1.68
  pts/session**, R² 0.37; in a joint fit the roll coefficient halves (−0.034 →
  −0.023) and the trend survives. Staleness is not it either — the October
  breaches sit at the ordinary 992–993 min age (10-12's 3874 is the weekend).
- **The pre-registered test — measure the breach against the same session's cash
  close — is possible on exactly one of the four, and it fails.** NDX cash closed
  **29950.82** on 10-14; the CFD closed **29931.8**; realised CFD-minus-cash basis
  at the close **−19.0**, against a scan-time board offset of **+41.8** — opposite
  sign, gap **60.8**.
- **Extended to the record** (prior-day cash close recovered from each brief's own
  `implied − roll`, paired with that day's CFD close from `review_day`): scan-time
  offset vs same-day realised close basis is **uncorrelated, r = −0.076, n = 20,
  mean |gap| 27.4**. *Caveat: the CFD session close is ~45 min after the 16:15 ET
  cash print, so the realised basis is noisy and this r is attenuated — not noisy
  enough to hide an effect of the size claimed.*

**NOTHING PROPOSED.** The offset is not measuring a CFD-vs-cash basis and it is
not a sell-off effect; tuning the conversion on a 13-point sample with r = +0.04
is the failure this register exists to prevent. The arithmetic was verified
independently on all three October breaches and was correct each time, and there
is no contract roll (NQ and NDX day-over-day agree within ~10pts), so this is not
the 09-24 failure mode. **Damage on 10-14: none** — price was 206.7 below the
flip, **4.9x** the offset. **Pre-registered:** log the realised close basis every
day (free; the NDX close is already fetched for the next morning's roll) and
re-test the trend at n=10 clean observations. `|px − flip| < |offset|` stays
**n=1** (10-12).

The 10-14 review's figures reproduce **exactly** (r = **+0.607**, slope
**+1.679**/session, R² **0.369**) on the sample it used: **n=27, first scan per
day, ex-09-24 — and already including 10-15's +77.6.** The trend was fitted on
the breach it was being used to explain. Extending the same sample:

| sample | n | r | R² | slope | resid SD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| thru 10-14 | 26 | +0.541 | 0.293 | +1.310 | 15.9 |
| thru 10-15 (the register's figure) | 27 | **+0.607** | 0.369 | +1.679 | 17.8 |
| **thru 10-16** | **28** | **+0.572** | **0.328** | **+1.499** | **18.0** |
| thru 10-16, 10-15 removed | 27 | +0.517 | 0.267 | +1.181 | 15.8 |

**Stated plainly, as directed: the trend survives as a description and fails as
an explanation, and the mechanism is still unexplained.**

- **Out of sample it misses both new points in opposite directions.** Fitted
  through 10-14 it predicts **31.1** for 10-15 (actual **77.6**, residual
  **+46.5**) and **32.4** for 10-16 (actual **14.9**, residual **−17.5**).

- The breach series is **four**: 09-28 **45.9** · 10-12 **43.1** · 10-14 **41.8**
  · 10-15 **77.6** (the 09-28 omission is corrected and stays corrected).

The sell-off hypothesis was falsified on 10-14; staleness is ruled out (992 min,
ordinary); a contract roll is ruled out (NQ and NDX day-over-day agree within
~10pts); and a monotonic drift cannot produce 77.6 followed by 14.9. **We do not
know what causes it. NOTHING PROPOSED, and no third story is substituted.**

the offset — **but total to the structural put wall**, which printed at −11.1

- **`expiry_shape: PIN_THEN_EXPAND` is NEW — confirmed against the whole

  **PRE-REGISTERED TEST, written before the outcome is known.** No ID taken, by
  the precedent of the 10-05 `SPIKE_THEN_REVERT` pre-registration, which is
  recorded under a prose heading with no number. The shape makes a **timing**
  claim, not a direction claim: *"Chop early, resolve late… breakouts will fail
  while the pin holds. From roughly 13:00 ET the pin weakens and the move that
  has been building gets released."*

  1. **Split the session at 17:00 UTC (13:00 ET).** Measure range and absolute
     net move in 13:30–17:00 UTC (pre) and 17:00–20:55 UTC (post).
  2. **CONFIRMED if** post-13:00 ET range **>** pre-13:00 ET range **AND** the
     session extreme on the side the day closes is made **after** 17:00 UTC.
  3. **FALSIFIED if** the pre-13:00 ET window holds the larger range, **OR** both
     the day's high and low are set before 17:00 UTC.
  4. **Secondary, for the "breakouts will fail" half:** count post-scan sweeps of
     the pre-scan high/low before 17:00 UTC and whether price closed back inside
     within 30 minutes. ≥1 sweep that reverses supports it; a sweep that runs is
     against.
  5. **Threshold: 3 `PIN_THEN_EXPAND` days.** At the observed frequency that is
     months away. **Nothing may be concluded from 10-19 alone**, and the first
     observation is to be recorded **without a verdict attached**.

## Journal hygiene

One scan file for 10-16 (`1248-preny.json` + `.md`), `is_trading_day: true`,
`review_day` reports **0 test artefacts** for the day (6 across the record,
excluded by `track.py`). **09-24 quarantined by hand — 14th consecutive review

H27 · D27 · P-I.**

The first three are *"gamma right, outvoted into a no-call"*. **10-20 is a
different cell: gamma wrong, outvoted into a directional call, and the outvote
was right.** The pre-registered quantity (sign and size of `gamma` minus the sum
of all other blocks, against `|post-scan|/ADR`) **still does not order the
outcome**: 9, 10, 6, **14** against 1.5x, 0.07x, 0.41x, **0.56x** — the largest
margin on record produced a mid-sized move. **n=1 in the directional cell.
Nothing proposed.**

**Decomposition of the −5, because only one half of it deserved to lose.**
`−3` location (*"below flip 30051.1 by 634.3pts — downside accelerates, rallies
unstable"*) was **half right**: the downside did accelerate (205.0pts through
three pools in 57 min) and the rally was **not** unstable (509.8pts in 45 min,
closed 18.4 off the high). One sign is scored for two claims. `−2` was the
**week net GEX** row — see H22. **The flip was 634.3pts = 1.20x ADR away**, so
the row's own escape clause (*"reclaim and hold above and fading becomes
valid"*) was unreachable by construction against a 202.9pt budget, and the board
still printed the flip as an actionable line.

## The duplication-collapse measurement, run across the whole record — and it does not support a weight change

Prompted by the 10-21 scan: **−7** with **−4 from a single FRED observation**
(DFII10 −3 + DGS10 −1) and **−2 from one UK CPI headline carried by two
outlets**, leaving **−1 of independent signal**. **Rules fixed in writing before
any outcome was inspected:** one PRE_NY `is_trading_day` scan per day, 09-24
excluded, 10-21 excluded as ungraded (**n=26 graded days / 19 calls**);
collapse (a) = DFII10/DGS10 become **one row, the larger |points| one kept**;
collapse (b) = duplicate scored headlines become **one event**, raw scaled by
`events / headlines`, `bias_points = clamp(round(raw/2), ±4)`.

| basis | C | W | no-call | rate | labels changed | sides changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **published** | 13 | 6 | 7 | **68.4%** | — | — |
| **collapse pair → 1 row** | 13 | **5** | 8 | **72.2%** | **4 / 26** | **1 / 26** |
| **drop the pair entirely** | 13 | **7** | 6 | **65.0%** | **21 / 26** | **7 / 26** |

- **The double-count is structurally real and large:** the pair contributes
  exactly **±4 on 29 of 34 scans** and ±1 on the other five; **|pair| ≥ |score|
  on 9 of 26 graded days**; on 10-20 **|pair|/|score| = 1.00**, i.e. the pair is
  the entire margin of the call.
- **It is nearly inert on direction.** The minimal dedup moves the printed label
  on 4 of 26 days and the **side on one** (09-30, WRONG → no-call). The
  3.8-point gain is **one day** — not evidence, nothing proposed.
- **The aggressive version is WORSE: 13/20 = 65.0%**, 3 helps (09-25 and 10-08
  no-call→correct, 09-30 wrong→no-call) against **4 hurts** (09-29 and **10-20**
  correct→no-call, 10-01 and 10-02 no-call→wrong). **An independent whole-sample
  confirmation that H18/P1's accuracy case stays RETRACTED.**
- **The headline half has never yet touched a graded day.** Duplicate scored
  headlines occur on **2 of 35 PRE_NY scans in the record**: **09-24**
  (quarantined) and **10-21** (ungraded). On 10-21 the collapse takes news
  **−2 → −1** and the score **−7 → −5** (`BEARISH → MILDLY BEARISH`). **H19's
  match-count defect is confirmed in its purest form and is, so far, a
  label-only effect — on a UK CPI story scoring the Nasdaq.**
- **Limitation, stated rather than hidden:** on **2 of 35** scans the published
  news table holds fewer rows than were scored (09-11 13:24 **10 scored / 6
  shown**; 10-05 **7 / 6**) and the journal stores no per-headline list, so
  duplicate detection there is **incomplete and unrecoverable**.

**Where it lands:** the implied fix is the **rendering** one — one row per FRED
observation, observation date on every row — which is **already PROPOSED under
H18 / P1** and was grepped for before this was written. **No number taken, no
weight change proposed**, because the measurement says a weight change makes the
record worse.

## H27 (NEW, OPENED) — the score's components are not independent, and collapsing them makes the record WORSE

**Opened 2026-10-26.** `grep -n "^## "` run first: **H27 · D28 · P-I** all
unused. Grepped for by claim before the number was taken — *collinear*,
*common cause*, *correlated component*, *double-count* — and nothing in the file
owns it. **H18/P1** is the DFII10/DGS10 pair and the rendering fix; **H19** is
duplicate headlines; the 10-21 whole-record duplication-collapse measurement
covers only those two. **H3** is CLOSED-NEGATIVE (*cap the conviction at range
extremes*) and is not this. **H26** is the magnitude-versus-direction claim —
**this entry is the MECHANISM behind H26, and that is why it is separable.**

**Claim.** The published score presents its blocks as independent evidence
(*"Driven by: vol −4 · gamma −3 · breadth −3 · structure −3 · rates −1 ·
macro −1 · news −1"*). They are not. Across all **33** PRE_NY `is_trading_day`
scans (09-24 and the unfinished 10-26 excluded), the Pearson correlation of
block subtotals is near zero for every pair except two:

| pair | r |
|---|---|
| **vol ↔ breadth** | **+0.533** |
| **structure ↔ gamma** | **+0.555** |
| structure ↔ rates | +0.206 (next largest) |
| all others | \|r\| ≤ 0.22 |

On the **13** days where the breadth row's prior-day NDX figure is recoverable
from the journal text, **vol r = +0.698** and **breadth r = +0.713** against that
same number. They are two readings of one event.

**10-23 is the extreme case.** Thursday's **−2.90%** NDX session was scored three
times — `vol −4` (VXN 28.72 **+17.6%**, VXN/VIX 1.44, VVIX 107.94: all
*consequences* of it), `breadth −3` (*"NDX −2.90% vs ES −0.44%"*: literally it),
`structure −3` (*"BELOW the entire prior-week range"*: where it put price).
**−13 of −16 came from the two collinear pairs. The independent remainder was
−3** — rates −1, macro −1, news −1 — i.e. **inside the engine's own ±3 deadband,
a no-call.** The 10-23 carry-forward note read this score as *"notably
broad-based… unlike 10-21 this score is NOT a duplication artefact"*. **That
reading is wrong, and the register made it** — it is a duplication artefact of a
kind the file was not watching for, and the FRED pair really did contribute only
−1, which is why looking there found nothing.

**PRE-REGISTERED TEST, rules fixed in writing before any outcome was
inspected** (10-21 duplication-collapse is the precedent): one PRE_NY
`is_trading_day` scan per day, 09-24 excluded, 10-26 excluded as unfinished
(**n=29 days / 22 calls**, the H26 sample); within each collinear pair, if both
subtotals share a **strict** sign, drop the member with the smaller |subtotal|;
deadband unchanged at |score| ≥ 3; **post-scan** grading per P-H.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| **published** | 13 | 9 | 7 | **59.1%** |

the window that gave **26.7 back**. No scoring row changes, no level changes;
the shape label and its mechanical description survive.

the page: a short-gamma *distance* term used as a *direction* term; a positive
0DTE gamma figure sitting two lines away, unused by the score but used by the
shape engine; a −6 whose independent content is **0**; a 27bp breadth spread

## D29 (NEW, OPENED) — the scan's session category and pre-scan window length are not constants

**Claim.** US clocks went back on **2026-11-01**. The Routine still fires at
**12:45 UTC**. `session_context.py:33–36` keys its windows to **ET hours**
(`LONDON` 3.0–8.5, `PRE_NY` 8.5–9.5), so a fixed-UTC trigger crosses the
boundary when the offset changes:

| | under EDT | under EST |
|---|---|---|
| 12:45–12:48 UTC in ET | 08:45–08:48 | **07:45–07:48** |
| `session_window` | `PRE_NY` | **`LONDON`** |
| minutes before NY cash open | ~42 | **~101** (the 11-02 brief's own figure) |

**Verified on disk:** `2026-11-02/1248-london.json`, `session_window: "LONDON"`,
`scan_et: "2026-11-02 07:48 ET (Mon)"` — against `*-preny.json` / `PRE_NY` on
every one of the 30-plus trading-day scans before it. Next DST change
**2027-03-14**, so **~93 trading days** of `LONDON` scans follow unless the
Routine time changes.

**Why it is a defect and not just a fact.** Nothing in the code or the register
guards against pooling the two populations, and the register's censuses are keyed
to `PRE_NY` **in prose**, where no assertion can fail.

**Consequences, recorded so no later reviewer pools them.**

1. **Censuses that stop accruing from 11-02:** the *"33 PRE_NY `is_trading_day`
   scans"* H27 was derived on, **P-B(b)**'s denominator (23), the
   **session-context field** census (22), and the pre-scan sweep counts.
   Widening any of them to include `LONDON` scans is a **change of population,
   not an extra observation.** The August note that *"early LONDON scans still
   run ~1.9x light"* on the fuel axis is direct evidence the two are **not**
   interchangeable.
2. **No CODE is blind to today's scan — checked.**
   `grep -rn "PRE_NY" --include=*.py` over the whole skill returns exactly two
   non-test hits: **`track.py:175`**, whose early-session list is
   `("ASIA", "LONDON", "PRE_NY")` and therefore **still captures** an 07:48 ET
   scan, and `session_context.py:36`, the window table itself. `review_day.py`
   reports `session_window` (line 246) and **never filters on it**. **The entire
   exposure is in this register's hand-maintained prose.**
3. **The record now holds THREE distinct pre-scan window lengths and they are
   not interchangeable:** the historical norm (~42 min before the open), the two
   late triggers (**10-27 ~26 min longer**, **10-30 ~32 min longer**), and
   **11-02 onward (~63 min longer still, same direction)**. Anything computed on
   `today_range`, `adr_used_pct`, `fuel_ratio`, `remaining_budget`, board offset
   or pre-scan contamination is a function of this length. **D29 absorbs the
   named late-trigger counter the 10-29 block asked for**, rather than taking a
   second number for one measurement axis: **late triggers 10-27, 10-30 (n=2);
   DST shift from 11-02 (n=1 and standing).**
4. **The fuel time-of-day baseline rebased CORRECTLY and that limb is sound.**
   11-02 printed *"ADR14 627.7, 37.9% used vs ~42% normal by 07:48 ET ->
   fuel_ratio 0.9"*. The arithmetic followed the clock; it is the
   **comparability of the resulting series** that breaks.

**D29 PROPOSES NOTHING.** No schedule change — **changing a Routine is the
user's to authorise and it was reported to them separately.** No code change. No
census is widened, narrowed or re-derived here.

**Status: OPEN, RECORD-ONLY.** Grepped before opening: `^## D29` unused;

(gradeable-day disagreement), **D26** (45-day window eating days from the back)

half-life**, for an event roughly **17 hours old**: **`news_scorer.py` ages the
HEADLINE, not the EVENT.**

prior-week range"*) and `breadth −1` (*"NDX −1.38% vs ES −1.12%"*) are
**consequences of that print**, not independent evidence about what comes next.

**Adjacent to H27 but NOT covered by it** — H27's measured pairs are

the competing reading — that the market was still repricing at 09:18 ET, and it

## D30 (NEW, OPENED and PROPOSED) — the 21:00Z roll constant no longer matches the broker's day, and the brief and the grader now disagree about one session's close by 83.1 points

**Claim.** `levels_fuel.py:90–94` buckets intraday bars on a **hard-coded
21:00 UTC**, with the docstring *"cTrader daily bars roll at 21:00 UTC"*. The
CFD session runs **18:00 → 17:00 ET**. Under EDT that ended at 21:00Z and the
constant was right. **Under EST it ends at 22:00Z**, so the boundary now falls
at **16:00 ET — exactly the NY cash close** — and cuts the session an hour early.

| | EDT (10-30) | **EST (11-02)** |
|---|---|---|
| bars in the graded day | 275 (22:00Z → 20:50Z) | **264 (23:00Z → 20:55Z)** |
| graded close | the 17:00 ET close | **the cash close** |
| post-close hour inside the graded day | 55 min | **0 min** |
| 21:00–22:00Z of 11-02 | — | bucketed into **`2026-11-03`**, its first 12 bars |

**Three consequences, each demonstrated from the tape, not inferred.**

1. **The post-close hour MIGRATED, it did not disappear.** The AAPL after-hours
   tape (21:00–22:00Z Nov 2: O 28002.7 / H 28112.6 / L 28002.0 / C 28085.6,
   range **110.6**, **+83.1**) carries `trading_day = 2026-11-03` and therefore
   inflates 11-03's `today_range` and `adr_used_pct` and deflates its
   `remaining_budget` — **the exact mechanism the 10-30 review challenged under
   H1/P4, relocated from the end of day D to the start of day D+1.**
2. **Two live definitions of the same session's close.** 11-03's board prints
   `PD close + PWL` at **28085.6** — the **21:55Z** close, from the **`D_1`**
   bar (`levels_fuel.py:173, 229`), which rolls at 22:00Z. `review_day` grades
   11-02's close as **28002.5** — the **20:55Z** close, from the
   `trading_day`-bucketed `M_5` series. **83.1 points apart.** `PDH 28754.5` /
   `PDL 27965.6` agree only by luck (the lost hour stayed inside the range).
   **`adr_used_pct` now divides a 21:00Z-bucketed numerator by a
   22:00Z-bucketed ADR14 denominator**, and that contamination grows as EST days
   enter the 14-day window.
3. **Friday's post-close hour will vanish entirely.**
   `trading_day(21:00Z Fri) → Saturday`, which has no scan and never enters a
   statistic. **First occurrence 2026-11-06.**

**PROPOSED: make the two day-definitions agree. Which roll is correct is the
user's call** — a DST-aware boundary tracking 17:00 ET, or an explicit
cash-close basis — and both have consequences for the back-record, so **no code
was edited.** **Status: OPEN, PROPOSED. D30 CORRECTS D29's point 2**
(*"No CODE is blind to today's scan — checked"*), whose grep covered only
`PRE_NY`. Grepped before opening: `^## D30` unused; **D29**, **D26**, **D1**,
**M7**, **D23** all checked, none covers the roll constant.

## M6 — THE DRIVER IS FOUND at session 37, and it is a one-line inversion

`review_day.py:159–161`, the `lost` branch of `grade_level`:

```python
react = (f"broke {'DOWN' if st['settled_side'] == 'above' else 'UP'} "
         f"through it — lost by {abs(st['worst_excursion']):.1f}pts")
```

`settled_read` sets `settled_side` from `bars[-1]["close"] >= price` — the side
price **ended on**. The ternary names the direction of the **adverse excursion
against** that side; the sentence *"broke X through it — lost by N"* reads as
**the direction the level broke**. **The two are always opposite.**

**Audited over every graded day the bar window serves: 82 of 82 lost-level rows
inverted, across the 25 sessions that had one, with `inverted == lost` on 30 of
30 days.** Not a statistic — an identity.

11-02 produced **8 inverted rows of 14 touched** on a day that closed 580 below
the scan, every one reading *"broke **UP** through it"* — including
**28084.6 PDL + PWL ⭐**, a floor that broke **down** by 119.0 and closed 82.1
below, reported as *"broke UP through it — lost by 36.5pts"*. **28711.5 NY High
contradicts itself inside one row** (`reaction` *"broke UP"* vs
`first_touch_reaction` *"broke DOWN"*). **10-28 produced 13 of 13.**

**The series is TWO defects, not one, and conflating them is why 37 sessions
found neither.** `_first_touch`'s fixed 12-bar window is a **separate, real**
defect — correct inside its window, misleading as a day verdict (10-30's PUT
WALL). The `held` branch (`support`/`resistance`) is **correct** and is not
implicated. The 10-30 attribution of the Asia-Low wording to the `settled_read`
**origin** defect is therefore **incomplete and is corrected here**.

**PROPOSED, to M6, no new ID** (grepped: M6 owns *"the grader's verdict is a
function of the session close"*). Two candidate forms — swap the ternary, or
re-word to *"settled below/above it after an N-point excursion the other way"*.
**The second is better** because it stops conflating the excursion with the
break. **This is grading code and it was NOT touched.**

## D31 (NEW, ALLOCATED and PROPOSED) — a close-to-close sigma compared to a high-low range

`brief.py:996` computes `implied = px * (vxn/100) / sqrt(252)` — a **1-sigma
close-to-close** daily move — then compares it directly to `f['adr14']`, a
**14-day average high-low range**, and gates *"options market prices a quieter
day, **use the smaller budget**"* on the comparison. **The document states the
rule it is breaking eight lines below**, for the straddle band: *"this is a
CLOSE-to-close band, not a high-low range. ADR measures high-low and is always
the larger number; comparing the two directly is the same error as reading the
range budget as price travel."* H8's entry (line 1032) has carried the identical
warning since 08-25.

- **10th counter-instance** to the gated instruction: VXN-implied **445.5**
  against a realised **1949.5**, under by **1504.0**. Preceded by 802.8 (11-04)
  and the series at lines 13377 / 14540 / 15075 / 15565 / 16160 / 17523.
  **Three consecutive sessions, same direction, increasing magnitude.**
- **Checked against my own case and it weakens it:** the `implied < adr14`
  branch is **not** near-unconditional — of 81 briefs on disk carrying the line,
  **58 took "below", 21 took "above", 2 neither** (VXN absent). The defect is
  the unit mismatch and the instruction, not the frequency.
- **Fix proposed is prose-only (a):** print the close-to-close caveat the
  straddle band already gets and **drop the `use the smaller budget`
  instruction**. Alternative (b), rescaling `implied` to a high-low comparable,
  is **declined** — the factor is unmeasured and that is tuning.
- **No score change, no board change, no budget change.**
- **ID checked first:** `^## D31`, `^## H28`, `^## P-J` all 0; no `^## ` heading
  matches `VXN|vol-implied|implied range`; the already-killed *"use the
  VXN-implied range as the budget"* idea is a different claim.

disjunct to P-F's trigger, on evidence of `budget == 0` being **4 of 4 positive
at mean +253.0** against **+17.7** for `budget > 0`.

coherence fix** (unnumbered, re-affirmed in unchanged wording): gate the fade
instruction on **below the flip ∩ negative weekly net GEX**, not on budget
magnitude.

## D22(a) — third limb: the blast radius is ENUMERATED, and `rates`/DXY is the bigger half

**The window mismatch is confirmed from source and the per-symbol blast radius —
the open question D22 posed on 2026-09-24 and never answered — is now closed.**

`macro_probe.py:58` `last = meta.get("regularMarketPrice") or closes[-1]`
against `macro_probe.py:64` `prev = closes[-2]`. On a ~24h symbol,
`regularMarketPrice` at 12:47Z is **today's live price** and `closes[-1]` is
**today's partial daily bar**, so `chg_pct` is **today's intraday move**. On a
cash index with no pre-market print, `regularMarketPrice` is the **stale prior
close**, so `chg_pct` is the **prior completed session**. The docstring at
`macro_probe.py:59-63` records fixing this exact class of bug for
`chartPreviousClose` and left the `last` line unfixed. `bias_engine.py:187-191`
differences two such legs as one sentence.

**Per-symbol enumeration.** Independent fetch 2026-11-10 ~12:55Z, comparing
`regularMarketPrice` against the dated daily closes the same call returns:

| symbol | dated bar for today? | `chg_pct` window | component |
|---|---|---|---|
| `^NDX` | no | prior session | `breadth` |
| `^VXN` | no | prior session | `vol` |
| `^TNX` `^FVX` `^IRX` | no | prior session | `rates` |
| `NVDA` `MSFT` `AAPL` `AVGO` | no | prior session | `breadth` |
| **`ES=F`** | **yes** | **today, live intraday** | `breadth` |
| **`DX-Y.NYB`** | **yes** | **today, live intraday** | `rates` |

**Exactly two of twelve symbols are affected**, and both are differenced against
prior-session legs **inside the same component**: `rates` mixes a prior-session
`^TNX` with a live DXY, `breadth` mixes prior-session mega-caps and `^NDX` with
a live ES.

**Point impact, five consecutive scans.** All legs from independent Yahoo daily
closes (`DX-Y.NYB` 11-03 101.87 / 11-04 101.51 / 11-05 101.55 / 11-06 102.30 /
11-09 101.65; `ES=F` 11-03 7596.75 / 11-04 7720.50 / 11-05 7383.00 / 11-06
7402.00 / 11-09 7574.25). **`^NDX` matched the prior completed session to 2dp on
all five scans — the NDX leg is not at issue, and this is also five clean
controls for D22(b), which stays SETTLED NEGATIVE.**

| scan | printed DXY | pts | prior-session DXY | pts | printed NDX/ES | pts | prior-session NDX/ES | pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11-04 | −0.55% | **+2** | +0.12% | 0 | +0.68 / +0.93 | **−1** | +0.68 / +0.29 | **+1** |
| 11-05 | +0.10% | 0 | −0.35% | 0 | +0.91 / +0.03 | **+1** | +0.91 / +1.63 | **−1** |
| 11-06 | +0.42% | **−2** | +0.04% | 0 | −6.36 / +0.22 | −1 | −6.36 / −4.37 | −1 |
| 11-09 | −0.41% | **+2** | +0.74% | **−2** | +1.35 / +0.67 | +1 | +1.35 / +0.26 | +1 |
| 11-10 | +0.12% | 0 | −0.64% | **+2** | +3.40 / −0.01 | +1 | +3.40 / +2.33 | +1 |

**DXY changes points on 4 of 5 scans, including a full 4-point sign flip on
11-09; breadth changes sign on 2 of 5, 2 points each. 10 of 10 leg-pairs are
mis-windowed by construction; 6 rows are point-changing.** The DXY gate is
`±0.4` (`bias_engine.py:150`) and the printed figures landed **0.01pp** under it
on 11-09 and **0.02pp** over it on 11-06 — a mixed window read through a
hair-trigger.

**Which leg to normalise — the evidence says LIVE, and that is NOT what the
correctness argument alone would give.** The breadth row recomputed with both
legs on the overnight window, using the NQ roll the brief **already computes and
prints** (`nq_implied`: 11-04 +128.0, 11-05 −229.0, 11-06 +399.0, 11-09 +166.2,
11-10 −106.8, against the prior cash close):

| scan | printed | prior-session | live/overnight | day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11-05 | +1 **wrong** | −1 right | **−1 right** | down hard |
| 11-06 | −1 **wrong** | −1 **wrong** | **+1 right** | +331.9 |
| 11-09 | +1 right | +1 right | **0 neutral** | +1045.5 |

**Live 2 right / 1 neutral / 0 wrong · printed 1 right / 2 wrong ·
prior-session 2 right / 1 wrong.** The whole-score check agrees: "both
prior-session" takes **11-09 from −3 to −7 — more confidently WRONG** — leaves
11-04 unchanged and moves 11-06 −19 → −17. It is **not** an accuracy
improvement. Live also leaves DXY alone, which is the only self-consistent
choice, since DXY cannot be made prior-session without discarding the overnight
FX move an intraday brief wants.

**PROPOSED, two parts:**

1. **Correctness, unconditional.** `yahoo_series` should return the window it
   measured and every consumer should print it. *"NDX x% vs ES y%"* and
   *"DXY n (±m%)"* assert a shared present tense they do not have. **n=5
   sessions, 6 point-changing rows, one 4-point sign flip.**
2. **Accuracy, weaker, n=3, direction of travel only.** Put the `breadth` NDX
   leg on the overnight window. **Zero new data:** `NQ=F` is on the same Yahoo
   endpoint and returned a live quote on the verification fetch (11-09 close
   28014.5 → 11-10 live 27892.25), and the brief already derives the number
   internally. Expected effect: breadth 1-right/2-wrong → 2-right/1-neutral
   across 11-05/11-06/11-09; score impact ±1 to ±2; **no label change on any of
   the three.**

**Falsifier for part 2:** three further sessions where the live-window breadth
row is wrong-signed and the printed row is right. **Record both variants every
scan.** Under this proposal the mega-cap average and `^TNX` stay prior-session
and become the remaining intra-component mismatch — **named, not proposed.**

**A new data point was named and DECLINED.** `ZN=F` is free and returned a live

**n=0. Watching: overnight ZN against the printed `^TNX` prior-session move,
every scan.**

   *"Strategy-1 fades have a materially lower hit rate here — only take them at

threshold met, read the evidence before proposing"*. That was treated as
actionable and the 3-session rule was applied by hand to every item above.
**Flagged rather than silently substituted for.**
